name: Question 19
problem: Let $f$ and $g$ be continuous functions such that ${\int }_{0}^{7}f(x)\,\text{d}x=18,{\int }_{0}^{7}\frac{1}{2}g(x)\,\text{d}x=5,$ and ${\int }_{3}^{7}(f(x)-g(x))\text{d}x=4.$ What is the value of ${\int }_{0}^{3}(f(x)-g(x))\text{d}x?$
worked_solution:
Let's simplify one of the given integrals:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{7}\frac{1}{2}\,g(x)\,\text{d}x & =5 \\ \frac{1}{2}{\int }_{0}^{7}g(x)\,\text{d}x & =5 \\ {\int }_{0}^{7}g(x)\,\text{d}x & =10\end{aligned}
$$

Then, using the adjacent intervals rule and substituting the known values, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{7}(f(x)-g(x))\text{d}x & ={\int }_{0}^{3}(f(x)-g(x))\text{d}x+{\int }_{3}^{7}(f(x)-g(x))\text{d}x \\ {\int }_{0}^{7}(f(x)-g(x))\text{d}x & ={\int }_{0}^{3}(f(x)-g(x))\text{d}x+4.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, by applying the sum rule for definite integrals and substituting the known values, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{7}(f(x)-g(x))\text{d}x & ={\int }_{0}^{3}(f(x)-g(x))\text{d}x+4 \\ {\int }_{0}^{7}f(x)\,\text{d}x-{\int }_{0}^{7}g(x)\,\text{d}x & ={\int }_{0}^{3}(f(x)-g(x))\text{d}x+4 \\ 18-10 & ={\int }_{0}^{3}(f(x)-g(x))\text{d}x+4 \\ 4 & ={\int }_{0}^{3}(f(x)-g(x))\text{d}x\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, ${\int }_{0}^{3}(f(x)-g(x))\text{d}x=4.$

∫07(f(x)−g(x))dx=∫03(f(x)−g(x))dx+4∫07f(x)dx−∫07g(x)dx=∫03(f(x)−g(x))dx+418−10=∫03(f(x)−g(x))dx+44=∫03(f(x)−g(x))dx
